name: Apple Silicon Mac, 32-64 GB unified (M1-M5 Pro/Max class)
notes: A wide class on purpose: 32 GB and 64 GB Macs behave differently, and bandwidth spans 68 GB/s (M1 8-core) to 546 GB/s (M4 Max). Reported numbers name the exact chip in the measurement note.
The binding constraint is RAM, not bandwidth: a 35B MoE at Q4 needs ~22 GB, which a 32 GB Mac runs with almost nothing left for context.
MoE expert streaming from SSD (mlx-flash style) is what makes over-RAM models possible here at a large speed cost.

memory.note: bandwidth is a per-chip property, so the class value stays null here and every variant carries its own; the class spans 68-546 GB/s end to end

compute.cpu_cores: Apple Silicon; core counts vary by chip and SKU tier
compute.note: Apple publishes Neural Engine TOPS but no GPU FLOPS for any M-series chip, so GPU compute stays null. Honest caveat for the MLX lanes: MLX and llama.cpp/Metal primarily drive the GPU; the Neural Engine is largely unused by current local-LLM runtimes, so its TOPS figure must not be read as an inference-throughput promise.

thermal.note: Apple does not publish chip TDP; sustained-load behaviour differs between fanless and fan-cooled enclosures

variants.name: M4 (base chip, 32 GB configs)
variants.note: Apple publishes 120 GB/s and a 16-core Neural Engine (38 TOPS) for the M4 family
